description: Walk from Cathedral Square to the River Nene, decoding a Restoration guildhall, royal burials and the city’s trading waterfront before a finish aboard a historic barge.
author: Day Tripping Quiz

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Raised on stone legs, I watched a king return while butter changed hands below. What am I?
stops.Hint_1: Search Cathedral Square for a small open-sided stone building.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the date 1671 above a structure raised on columns.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Old Guildhall is dated 1671 and is Grade II* listed. Its open ground floor served as a market space, placing civic business above the bustle of Cathedral Square.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the square, count the visible ground-floor arches or note the date displayed on the building.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Three great arches guard the resting places of one queen and the former grave of another.
stops.Hint_1: Walk towards the cathedral and face its monumental west front.
stops.Hint_2: Look for three enormous Gothic arches beneath matching gables.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Peterborough Cathedral’s west front is famous for its three vast Gothic arches. Katharine of Aragon is buried inside, while Mary, Queen of Scots rested at Peterborough for twenty-five years before James I moved her remains to Westminster Abbey.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look up safely from the precinct and note one repeated shape or figure across the three gables.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Beside the Nene, a little house once watched cargo arrive and made river traders pay their dues.
stops.Hint_1: Follow public pavements south towards Town Bridge and the river.
stops.Hint_2: Find the small historic building beside the north side of the bridge.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Old Customs House recalls Peterborough’s working waterfront, when tolls and duties were collected from goods arriving by barge on the River Nene. The building is viewed from outside.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the public path, note one feature that makes this small building look different from the modern riverside structures.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: My deck once carried grain across European canals; now I stay moored where the Nene meets Town Bridge.
stops.Hint_1: Stay beside the river and look for a large converted barge.
stops.Hint_2: Find the floating venue called Charters on the west side of Town Bridge.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! Charters occupies the converted Dutch barge Leendert-R, built in 1907 and used to carry cargo on European waterways until 1990. Enjoy the riverside finish if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the public riverside, notice one surviving working-boat feature on the barge’s exterior.

short_description: Decode royal, civic and river-trade stories from the cathedral to the Nene.

before_you_go.terrain: Paved city-centre streets, Cathedral Square and riverside paths, ending beside a moored barge.
before_you_go.hills: The route is largely level, with bridge approaches and ordinary dropped-kerb gradients.
before_you_go.steps: No steps are needed to reach the outdoor checkpoints; access aboard the final barge uses its current gangway arrangements.
before_you_go.accessibility: All clues can be solved from public, outdoor routes. Riverside surfaces, bridge works and the barge gangway can change, so check current access if step-free travel is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current city-centre or cathedral visitor-facility listings before departure; facilities at the finish depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable shoes with grip are sensible for paving that may be wet beside the river.
before_you_go.dogs: Dogs can accompany the outdoor route on a lead; check Charters Bar’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: The outdoor route is generally pushchair-friendly, but the final gangway and temporary riverside works may need extra care.

recommended_age: Recommended 12+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A compact city-centre route from Cathedral Square to Town Bridge and the River Nene.
